final_message:
All 17 tests pass (6 visible + 11 new regression tests), and I independently re-verified every docstring contract.

## Files changed

**`workspace/inventory/pricing.py`**
- `parse_price`: docstring promised `"$1,299.50"` and `"(12.00)"` but the code only stripped `$`, so thousands separators raised `InvalidOperation` and parentheses were ignored. Now strips `,` and turns accounting-style parentheses into a negative Decimal.
- `apply_discount`: `quantize()` used the default banker's rounding, so `10.05` at 10% gave `9.04` instead of the documented half-up `9.05`. Now quantizes with `ROUND_HALF_UP` (and accepts float percentages safely via `Decimal(str(...))`).

**`workspace/inventory/report.py`**
- `low_stock`: used `qty <= threshold` (spec says *strictly below*) and returned names in input order (spec says alphabetical, case-insensitive). Now uses `<` and `sorted(..., key=str.lower)`.

**`workspace/inventory/export.py`**
- `to_csv_row`: never quoted names, contradicting its RFC 4180 docstring. Now wraps names containing a comma or double quote in quotes and doubles inner quotes.

**Annotations**: the repo-conventions rule requires public functions to be fully annotated, so all public functions gained parameter and return annotations (`str -> Decimal`, `Decimal, float -> Decimal`, `Iterable[Mapping[str, Any]] -> Decimal`, `-> list[str]`, `Mapping[str, Any] -> str`).

**`workspace/tests/test_regressions.py`** (new; existing tests untouched) — one regression test per fixed bug: thousands separator, accounting negatives, half-up rounding, strict-below threshold, case-insensitive sorting, comma quoting, and inner-quote doubling.

**`workspace/CHANGELOG.md`** — four entries under `## Unreleased`, one per fix, in the existing bullet format.
